headline: CORN RALLIES ON CHINA HOPES; CATTLE JUMP 2.4%
lead: Corn ran 15 cents to three-week highs and beans gained 24 cents overnight on fresh hope for a US-China trade deal, but both gave it back into the close, corn settling $5.38 and beans $13.19, both down on the day. Cattle didn't fade: $221.15, up 2.4% on record low placements.
teaser: Corn and beans faded a China-hope rally; cattle didn't, closing up 2.4% on record low placements.

one_number.unit: India's YoY crude import bill increase
one_number.context: India paid $24.4 billion more for crude April-August despite buying 0.4% less volume, that's the diesel and input-cost pressure showing up somewhere other than the US pump.

yesterdays_call.note: Crude closed $89.80, down 3.4% on the day, not the level called, but Iran diplomacy hope is now pushing it back up, not down.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called crude down toward $91.50 ($92.97 when the call was made). It closed at $89.8.

action: Live cattle at $221.15: nothing to sell into a 2.4% up day off record low placements, hold for $222 confirmation.

sections.title: Grains Fade The China Pop
sections.body:
- Corn rallied over 15 cents and beans gained 24 cents overnight on hopes for a US-China trade deal, then both gave it back, corn settling **$5.38** and beans $13.19, both down on the day.
- That's a classic buy-the-rumor, sell-the-fact pattern under China's $17 billion annual purchase commitment, headlines move the screen, follow-through is another question.
sections.so_what: The overnight pop was the story; the close erased it.

sections.title: Cattle Ignore The Grain Fade
sections.body:
- Live cattle closed **$221.15**, up 2.4%, decoupling completely from the soft grain tape on record low September placements into feedlots.
- AgWeb is already asking if this pulls fund buying into the complex; feeders followed at $337.80, up 1.3%.
sections.so_what: Cattle trading its own supply story, ignoring grain and crude entirely.

sections.title: Crude Reverses On Iran Hope
sections.body:
- WTI closed **$89.80**, down 3.4%, but that's a session where crude reversed higher late on hope for US-Iran diplomacy ahead of the UN General Assembly.
- The Iran-Hormuz cycle, a July re-escalation that's since cooled, is getting another headline test; Treasury is threatening to ground Iranian airlines, which cuts the other way.
sections.so_what: Crude and diesel are still decoupled; today's headlines don't change fuel bills.

outside_the_pit.title: Saudi Aramco May Reopen Yanbu Port to Asian Refiners
outside_the_pit.body: Aramco is telling refiners they can pick up cargoes at Yanbu again soon, a crude-supply signal that could pressure the deflating Hormuz premium further.

watch_list.desc: Beef Magazine fall/winter weather webinar; drought outlook shift changes fall fieldwork math.
Cattle above $222 pulls fresh fund money in; below $219 says today's pop was a one-day squeeze.
Corn holding above $5.35 keeps the China-hope bid alive; a close under it says the rally was rumor only.
